messages:
SRE-Bot: [ALERT] High unhealthy target count detected for ALB 'alb-edge-azb' (us-east-1 / azb). Metric spike at 03:12 UTC — unhealthy_targets > 70% across target-group tg-0a1b2c3. Auto-escalation to on-call.

Nina (oncall): Acked. I'm jumping in. Any immediate customer reports?

Priya (CS Lead): Getting pings from 3 customers about 502s and slow page loads. Looks concentrated on east coast users.

Nina (oncall): Running quick health check against a few targets, attaching logs.

Nina (oncall): ```bash
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456789012:targetgroup/tg-0a1b2c3/abcdef012345 --region us-east-1
```

Nina (oncall): sample output shows repeated Unhealthy -> Initializing -> Unhealthy cycles for many hosts (TargetHealth: {State: "unhealthy", Reason: "Health checks failed"}).

Marcus (network): Seeing increased health-check latency on probe path from ALB to instance ENIs in azb. Packet traces show intermittent 504s between ELB and instance ports.

Ayesha (platform): Are these instances under heavy CPU or IO? Could be EBS latency cascading into failed app probes.

Nina (oncall): Checked: CPU ~20-30%, but `iowait` spikes correlate with probe failures. Running `iostat -x 1 5` on a few instances shows occasional high await on /dev/nvme1n1.

Nina (oncall): Quick curl to edge VIP shows 502s from the ALB early in the window:
```bash
curl -I https://edge.example.com/health || true
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 03:13:02 GMT
```

Tom (SRE Lead): This looks like a cross-layer degradation: EBS IO spikes causing app slow responses -> ALB health check timeouts -> unhealthy target oscillation. Could be a noisy neighbour or underlying AZ storage issue.

Marcus (network): I'm seeing similar probe timeouts to other AZs but only azb has persistent 5xx. azc/aze fine.

Nina (oncall): Immediate mitigation options: 1) Temporarily reduce weight to azb in Route53 weighted policy; 2) Increase ALB healthy threshold / healthcheck timeout to avoid flapping; 3) Drain and replace unhealthy instances in azb; 4) Open AWS case. Thoughts?

Ayesha (platform): Do 1 + 4 now. We want traffic reduced quickly. Also prepare to scale up in other AZs if needed. I'll run a Canary policy to shift 20% to azc then 80% to azd if needed.

Nina (oncall): Making Route53 change: setting weighted records so azb goes from weight 100 -> 10 for alias edge.example.com (TTL 30). Pushing now.

SRE-Bot: Route53 change propagated (API change-id r53-change-zzxy). New weights: azb=10, azc=45, azd=45.

Priya (CS Lead): Notifying affected customers: sent slim update to customers A,B,C noting degraded performance in east coast and we are routing around problem.

Nina (oncall): Opening AWS Support case now with EC2/EBS/ELB logs and timelines. Case ID: 1234567890. Adding diagnostics: iostat snippets, ELB target health dumps, packet captures.

AWS Support Bot: Case 1234567890 created. Assigned to SE. Initial response ETA ~ 30 minutes.

Marcus (network): While support engages, I'm going to cordon azb instances from autoscaling group and spin up replacements in azd/azc. Running ASG detach for instances with unhealthy tags.

Nina (oncall): Running drain command on ALB for flagged instances: ```bash
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn <arn> --targets Id=i-0abc12345 --region us-east-1
```

Nina (oncall): After deregistering, ALB target counts decreased and 502 rate dropped by ~9% within 3 minutes. Traffic to azb now ~8% per R53 weights.

Tom (SRE Lead): Good. Keep draning noisy instances. Also update health-check settings temporarily: increase timeout from 5s -> 8s and healthy threshold from 3 -> 5 to reduce flapping. We revert after AWS confirms root cause.

Ayesha (platform): I applied the ALB healthcheck change via config rollout (canary 50%). Monitor for any adverse effects.

Nina (oncall): Monitoring: error rate from azb continuing to decline. Global 5xx rate down from 12% -> 3%. Still seeing occasional spikes every ~10m.

Marcus (network): AWS SE responded: they're seeing storage backend degradation in a set of EBS hosts in the AZ that correlate with IO spikes. Their mitigation is to migrate volumes off impacted hardware; will provide timeline.

AWS Support Bot: Update to case 1234567890: SE confirms 'network-adjacent EBS substrate degradation' affecting some instances in us-east-1azb. AWS plan: volume migration in waves (ETA 2-3 hours for full remediation).

Priya (CS Lead): Messaging update: posting to status page that a regional EBS substrate issue is impacting a subset of instances in us-east-1/azb. Temporary traffic shift and instance replacements in progress. ETA preliminary: 2-3 hours.

Nina (oncall): Since remediation is multi-hour, switching to longer-term mitigations: 1) increasing cross-AZ capacity for autoscaling groups; 2) setting permanent low weight for azb until AWS confirms fixed; 3) scheduling post-incident instance replacements. Implementing autoscaling now.

Ayesha (platform): Kicking off ASG scale-up in azc/azd by +30% capacity. Also ensuring new instances mount fresh EBS volumes (avoid reusing possibly degraded volumes).

Marcus (network): Note: we saw a daisy-chain effect where ALB health probes triggered connection retries which saturated some NAT gateways in azb. We should monitor NAT GW queue depths — I moved some proxy NATs to spare capacity.

Tom (SRE Lead): Good catch. Add NAT-GW saturation to the incident notes.

Nina (oncall): Quick status update for channel: Route53 weights changed, ALB healthchecks relaxed, bad instances drained, ASGs scaled in other AZs, AWS is migrating EBS volumes. 5xx rate down to 1.8% globally.

Priya (CS Lead): Customers updated. We also offered temporary traffic routing guidance to large customers wanting immediate failover (they accepted).

AWS Support Bot: Case 1234567890: AWS completed migration for a subset of affected volumes at 05:40 UTC. They will continue rolling. Please confirm if you want them to aggressively move remaining volumes (may cause brief IO hiccups).

Nina (oncall): Let's let them do the aggressive migration during our daytime window — approve immediate remainder. Noted potential short hiccups.

Marcus (network): After approval, we observed a 30-minute window of small IO spikes but health stabilized afterwards. Now steady.

Tom (SRE Lead): Start timeline capture. Nina, please keep running regular dumps of ELB target health and EBS CloudWatch metrics every 10m and attach to the case and incident doc.

Nina (oncall): Will do. Also creating post-incident ticket to triage: root cause RCA, why NAT GW saturated, pre-warming autoscaling responses, and runbook updates for weighted failover. Assigning to Platform team.

Priya (CS Lead): Preparing customer-facing postmortem summary for impacted SLAs. ETA 6 hours for draft.

Nina (oncall): Last check: global 5xx back to baseline (0.2%), health targets stable, azb target health steady at 95% healthy. Changing Route53 weights back to even (azb -> 33, azc -> 33, azd -> 34) with TTL 60.

SRE-Bot: Route53 change propagated (change-id r53-change-yyzz).

Tom (SRE Lead): Great work. Incident declared resolved for operational impact at 06:20 UTC. Followups: postmortem owner: Ayesha, timeline owner: Nina, customer comms: Priya, AWS liaison: Marcus.

Priya (CS Lead): I'll post the customer note that it's resolved and we'll follow up with a postmortem.

AWS Support Bot: Case 1234567890: Case closed after volume migrations completed. If further anomalies appear, reopen and contact assigned SE.

Nina (oncall): Closing the incident thread in channel. Logging all artifacts to incident tracker. Thanks everyone. :tada:
